ranked.headline: Pretrained models on cfDNA, cfRNA and proteomes are yielding disease biomarkers
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs large pretrained models with cell-free nucleic acid and plasma proteomic data for disease detection and chronic risk prediction.

ranked.headline: Correcting and replacing read-based transcript quantification with orthogonal checks
ranked.summary: Read-level quantification is being re-examined for normalization bias, reference dependence, and agreement with long-read and protein measurements.

ranked.headline: Simulations show ligand and salt conditions reshape condensates and protein states
ranked.summary: Current simulations and kinetic models tie salt, ligands, and membrane interfaces to condensate behavior and single-protein dynamics.

ranked.headline: Structure web servers couple AlphaFold models with docking, MD, and stability prediction
ranked.summary: Eight published servers and one preprint extend structural analysis to SAXS, docking, glycosylation, and metal-site prediction.

ranked.headline: Spatial multi-omics models reconstruct and translate single-cell tissue architecture
ranked.summary: Recent work extends single-cell and spatial models to cross-omics translation, 3D reconstruction, and histology-based expression prediction.

ranked.headline: Computational tools infer microbial gene functions from metagenomes and pangenomes
ranked.summary: CAZyOGH annotates glycoside hydrolases in unassembled metagenomes, and Microbe Decoder combines several inference routes to predict microbial functional traits.

ranked.headline: Integrating heterogeneous evidence into interpretable variant and gene-level predictions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications return variant and gene predictions with their contributing evidence attached, rather than as opaque scores.

ranked.headline: Learned models now generate and predict peptides, macrocycles, and protein variants
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers apply flow, all-atom, and language-model frameworks to macrocycles, peptides, and enzymes.

ranked.headline: Inferring latent cell-state dynamics from single-cell and spatial measurements
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial datasets now support inference of fitness, directionality, and ancestry with explicit uncertainty treatment.

ranked.headline: Developability and target identity treated as design inputs in molecular optimization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply developability, affinity and fitness criteria directly inside design and screening workflows.

ranked.headline: Web servers for structure search, pocket flexibility and atomic charge calculation
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 publications deliver web-accessible tools for structure search, ensemble pocket analysis, charge assignment and peptide editing.

ranked.headline: Transformer and graph models advance gene expression and regulatory network inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply transformer, graph, and diffusion learning to spatial, single-cell, and regulatory omics data, with new benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Structure models extend to RNA, antibodies, TCR-peptide-MHC and kinase complexes
ranked.summary: Benchmarks of AlphaFold 3 on TCR, antibody, RNA and ubiquitinated-protein tasks show uneven performance across application areas.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-resolved eukaryotic genomes from long reads expose ploidy and genus evolution
ranked.summary: Long-read and HiFi data now yield gapless, chromosome-level references, enabling comparative analyses of ploidy, repeats and pangenomes across lineages.

ranked.headline: Sequence models predict regulatory activity, mutation risk and enhancer-gene links
ranked.summary: Sequence-to-function models now span base-pair mutation risk, m6A sites, chromatin state and enhancer-gene maps across cell types.

ranked.headline: Interaction networks give molecular features causal and topological meaning
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and tools embed radiation, cancer, and multiomic measurements in directed or topological networks to assign functional context.

ranked.headline: SQLite-backed indexed formats enable disk-based subgraph access to pangenome graphs
ranked.summary: Preprint formats make pangenome graphs and alignments queryable on disk, while a published toolkit extends metadata-driven SQL access to hologenome resources.

ranked.headline: Language models adapted to protein, genomic and single-cell biology across modalities
ranked.summary: A 52.6B-token biology pre-training corpus and several multimodal protein and genomic models appeared in July 2026 preprints.

ranked.headline: Equivariant and generative deep learning models for molecules and protein dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair equivariant architectures with ab initio-level labels and MD-derived training data for drugs, proteins, and complexes.

ranked.headline: Single-cell maps define cell states in wounds, aging lung, and immune responses
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial maps now resolve conserved wound states, lung aging hallmarks, and immune response programs at atlas scale.

ranked.headline: Prediction tools nominate regulators, biosensor ligands and metal-site dehydrogenases
ranked.summary: July 2026 items pair structure-based metal-site screening with web servers predicting regulators and biosensor ligands.

ranked.headline: Refining spectral libraries and standardizing coordinates to curate quantitative MS data
ranked.summary: Library refinement, retention-time indexing and coordinate standardization now shape quantitative interpretability across DIA, CE-HRMS and structural data.

ranked.headline: Protein language models gain from domain pretraining, augmentation and frozen embeddings
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a July 2026 publication test how pLM design, training data and embedding reuse affect predicted fitness and ΔΔG ranking.

ranked.headline: Sequencing analysis tools combine modalities to extract more information per run
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers extend somatic calling, Perturb-seq analysis, and CRISPR reagent design to richer sequencing and perturbation data.

ranked.headline: Lipid Composition and Allosteric Coupling in Membrane-Anchored Signaling Complexes
ranked.summary: Current simulations link allosteric communication to lipid composition and gating residues in receptors, GTPase complexes, and C2 domains.

ranked.headline: Variant effect predictors add patient context and face scrutiny of attributions
ranked.summary: Integrative and foundation-model variant predictors are now appearing, prompting scrutiny of their attributions and cross-species transfer.

ranked.headline: Atom-level uncertainty localizes failure structures in molecular property prediction
ranked.summary: Recent evaluations show scaffold splits understate OOD error, making calibrated uncertainty a diagnostic requirement for molecular property models.

ranked.headline: Phosphoproteomics and pan-cancer proteomics feed web-based network and enrichment analyses
ranked.summary: Phosphosite-resolved and pan-cancer proteomic datasets are now being packaged into browser-based analysis workflows.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomes link lineage traits to regulatory and mutational evolution
ranked.summary: Multi-species genome sequencing and alignment now connect mutation, regulatory, and life-history variation to evolutionary and geographic history.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomes reveal lineage-specific selection and repeat turnover
ranked.summary: Pangenome, multi-genome, and genome-wide cline approaches now resolve lineage-specific variation in selection, repeat content, and barrier loci.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict patient outcomes from sparse, heterogeneous clinical data
ranked.summary: Four 2026 preprints apply transformers, VAEs, generative models and LLM agents to incomplete multimodal patient data for prognosis and trajectory modeling.

ranked.headline: Port-Hamiltonian digital twins of neural and circadian dynamics show partial fidelity
ranked.summary: Physics-structured digital twins are now fitted to EEG and multi-omics data, exposing where structural priors help and where they fall short.

ranked.headline: Free web servers predict RNA structure, protein localization, and TF binding effects
ranked.summary: Five 2026 publications package structural and sequence-context features into freely accessible servers for predicting molecular function.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein encoders reused across enzyme, peptide and antigen prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent items pair pretrained ProtT5 or ProtBERT embeddings with attention, gated and graph architectures for peptide, enzyme and tumor antigen prediction.

ranked.headline: Conditioned generative models tuned with RL for disease-aware small-molecule design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a journal article pair context-conditioned molecular generators with multiobjective optimization for structure- and disease-aware design.

ranked.headline: Software tools for reproducible omics, privacy-preserving genomics, and cfDNA screening
ranked.summary: Three recent open-source tools address reproducibility, collaborative privacy, and clinical liquid biopsy analysis in omics workflows.

ranked.headline: Computational deconvolution resolves chromatin and damage readouts along biological axes
ranked.summary: Pooled and genome-wide epigenomic readouts now demand computational models that separate genotype, cell-cycle, and TF-mediated effects.

ranked.headline: Web Servers move primer design and viral contig discovery into browser-based workflows
ranked.summary: Recent browser-facing tools package established sequence analysis steps and extend them to viral discovery in metagenomes and transcriptomes.

ranked.headline: Reference-quality genomes and protein-family resources for fungal and arthropod systems
ranked.summary: New chromosome-level and near-complete assemblies plus a protein-family database extend genomic resources for fungi and arthropods.

ranked.headline: Sensing, consumption and geometry jointly shape collective chemotactic front formation
ranked.summary: Recent models and agent-based experiments link coupled fronts and geometry-dependent reversal of chemorepulsion to collective chemotaxis outcomes.
